extracted.intended_audience: Congress, federal agencies, electric cooperative leaders, policymakers, and NRECA members
extracted.subtask_description: News/advocacy reporting and policy recommendations from NRECA focused on ensuring reliable, affordable electric service for co-op members by reforming permitting, regulation, funding, supply chains, and infrastructure investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize reliable, affordable power
rubrics_metrics.description: American families and businesses expect the lights to stay on at a cost they can afford; energy policies must meet this fundamental expectation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and regulatory decisions should be evaluated primarily on whether they preserve or enhance reliability and affordability for consumers. Statements in the piece repeatedly assert reliability and affordability as the North Star for co-ops.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support a diverse supply of energy resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Support a diverse supply of energy resources to meet escalating demand for U.S. energy production and manufacturing, especially in rural areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include planning new natural gas power plants, wind turbine repowering, and transmission projects. The article frames a 'balanced approach' — combining multiple resource types — as ensuring reliable, affordable and environmentally responsible energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve and streamline environmental permitting processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve environmental permitting processes and cut costly, burdensome regulations to accelerate deployment and maintenance of critical electric infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for permitting reform to cut down long delays (permits can take six or seven years), speed environmental reviews, and allow greater applicant involvement. Bipartisan permitting legislation is highlighted as a path to modernization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curb lengthy, costly litigation that delays projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress should curb lengthy, costly litigation that can cause unnecessary and often indefinite delays that hold up projects communities need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Litigation is identified as a source of indefinite project delays; policy measures should reduce frivolous or prolonged litigation that impedes infrastructure buildout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure federal programs and resources run efficiently and effectively for co-ops
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure federal programs and resources that support electric co-op energy projects are run efficiently and effectively as co-ops invest to meet community needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal funding programs (USDA, DOE, etc.) should be administered so funds actually support grid hardening, modernization, and other co-op projects without unnecessary inefficiency or delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid or repeal unworkable or unlawful regulations (specifically EPA power plant rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate what NRECA believes are unlawful and unachievable regulations, including the EPA power plant greenhouse gas rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA rule is criticized for mandating unproven technology and unachievable emissions limits, potentially forcing premature plant closures and jeopardizing affordable, reliable electricity. The article urges repeal or replacement with cost-effective, lawful requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations should be technologically demonstrated and achievable
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal regulations should not mandate inadequately demonstrated technology or unachievable emissions limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRECA argues the power plant rule would require costly carbon capture technology not adequately demonstrated at commercial scale; rules must be demonstrably implementable and costed to avoid large rate impacts (example: estimated 60% rate increase for Basin Electric members by 2035).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect co-ops’ access to direct-pay tax credits and equitable incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Protect co-ops’ access to direct-pay tax credits, which allow co-ops to leverage federal energy incentives to help fund innovative infrastructure projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically investor-owned utilities have benefited more from tax incentives; ensuring co-ops can access direct-pay credits is framed as necessary for parity and to finance projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support and preserve targeted grant/loan programs for co-ops (e.g., New ERA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Congress should support USDA and co-ops as they deploy projects and oppose any cuts to the New Empowering Rural America (New ERA) program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New ERA is described as a voluntary grant and loan program designed specifically for electric co-ops for projects like nuclear, carbon capture, batteries, and renewables; NRECA urges continued funding and opposition to cuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan and invest to meet projected load growth
rubrics_metrics.description: Utilities and co-ops should plan capital investments (example: Basin Electric plans $12 billion over the next decade) based on projected load growth to serve members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investment decisions are justified by specific load growth projections (Basin Electric 3.3% vs national 2.4%) and identified drivers (cryptocurrency, data centers, ethanol-related CCS, local economic development). Policy should enable and support such investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make effective use of existing infrastructure funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Make effective and efficient use of remaining infrastructure funding from Congress and maintain other key federal funding programs for co-ops.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to DOE and USDA awards and loans (e.g., $579M USDA award, DOE funding for batteries) illustrate using federal funds to expand renewables, storage, and refinance assets; funds should be applied to maximize grid resilience and affordability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cut regulatory 'red tape' at land and species management agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut red tape at land and species management agencies that hinders co-ops’ work to build and maintain electric systems in federal areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Streamlining land-use and species-related processes is framed as essential to reduce delays on projects crossing federal lands; proposals include coordination and procedural reform to remove unnecessary obstacles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boost domestic manufacturing and supply chains for critical grid equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Support legislation and incentives (e.g., tax credits) to boost U.S. production of distribution transformers and other critical equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CIRCUIT Act (10% tax credit) is cited as a means to strengthen domestic supply chains for transformers; manufacturers report they would redeploy capital to grow output if credits pass, improving resiliency and speed of equipment delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design transmission projects to minimize environmental impacts and use mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: When building transmission, co-locate within existing rights-of-way where possible, provide opportunity for public comment, and implement mitigation and restoration measures to minimize environmental impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: More than 95% of Cardinal-Hickory Creek line was co-located within existing ROW; project used mitigation/restoration and public engagement to ease permitting and environmental concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission planning should increase redundancy and reduce congestion
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmission upgrades should reduce grid congestion, increase reliability and voltage strength, and provide contingency feeds to reduce risk of load loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include the Cardinal-Hickory Creek and Basin Electric 345-kV projects which are credited with improving regional reliability, enabling renewable interconnection, and providing contingency benefits to serve growing demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate early and broadly with stakeholders (tribes, counties, utilities, regulators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective project delivery requires coordination with county/regulatory bodies, utility partners, pipeline operators, and tribal leadership during design and construction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Basin Electric line credits local counties, the ND Public Service Commission, pipeline operators and tribal leadership for facilitating approvals and navigation around existing utilities; stakeholder cooperation is presented as a success factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage generator retirements and ensure sufficient reliability services
rubrics_metrics.description: Market operators and authorities should carefully manage generator deactivations and ensure sufficient reliability services as plants retire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC recommends careful management of deactivations and ensuring reliability services; policy should address replacement capacity and services to avoid shortfalls as dispatchable resources exit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline interconnection processes for new resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure new resources can interconnect effectively and reliably into the grid so they actually deliver capacity when needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article cites interconnection bottlenecks and the need to ensure that resources in queues (often solar, battery, hybrid) can connect and contribute reliably; siting/permitting reforms should include interconnection improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educate policymakers and regulators on reliability implications of policy choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Policymakers and regulators need education on how energy policy decisions affect grid reliability during and after transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NERC and NRECA stress that policy-driven transitions present reliability risks; increasing awareness among decision-makers is presented as a critical need to avoid unintended reliability consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue bipartisan, pragmatic permitting reforms to keep pace with global competitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitting reform should be bipartisan and practical so the U.S. does not fall behind other nations in generating capacity and infrastructure deployment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes from lawmakers and NRECA leaders emphasize urgency and cross-party interest; goal is a more rational, reasonable process applicable across energy types to accelerate project timelines.
